title: Universal Protocol v1 — Operations
description: Request/response operations. Each request carries a scope requirement; nodes enforce scope on every operation. Reconnect/replay is a first-class operation (session.replay) so clients recover missed events deterministically.

lastEventId.description: Client's last seen event id; null for a fresh client.

NodeHello.description: Greeting sent by the node on every new connection, before the client authenticates. Carries the nonce the client must sign, and the identity the client verifies against its pairing record.

challengeB64.description: Nonce the client signs with its paired device private key for auth.connect. Single-use per connection.

operations.description: The operation set this node actually serves. Clients use it for capability discovery; operations absent from it are CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED at dispatch time.

platform.description: The node's host platform (Phase 3B). A controller uses this, with nodeKind, to decide which capabilities to offer before its first request.

nodeKind.description: desktop or android. An android node is supervised by the Android runtime and never advertises terminal or update operations.

AuthConnect.description: Client authentication. Proves possession of the paired device private key by signing the node.hello challenge. A pairing token alone is never accepted here; the token is only consumed by device.pair.

sigB64.description: Signature over the node.hello challengeB64 with the device long-lived private key.

requestedScopes.description: Subset request; the node may grant less than asked and records exactly what it granted.

AuthConnectResponse.description: Successful authentication result. Grants are authoritative: the client must use the granted scope set, not what it requested.

sessionId.description: Omit to create a new session; supply to continue an existing one. A sessionId the node has not seen is adopted into the session index (registered with this project) so Project → Session → Task stays unambiguous.

provider.description: Provider profile name; null = node default.

clientRequestId.description: Optional idempotency key. The same authenticated device re-sending the same semantic request with the same clientRequestId receives the SAME task, never a duplicate. The same id with a materially different request is rejected with CONFLICT. Idempotency records live in the durable task store and are retained for the node's event-log retention window.

TaskStartResponse.description: Task accepted. state is the task's actual state when the reply is written ('queued' for a fresh task; the current state for an idempotent replay).

idempotentReplay.description: true when this reply returns an existing task created by an earlier identical request with the same clientRequestId.

TaskCancelRequest.description: Requests node-side cancellation: SIGTERM (bounded) then force kill. The node records the outcome; the client learns it from the task.cancelled event, not from this response.

state.description: Filter to tasks in this state.

TaskHistoryRequest.description: Returns the node-owned durable event timeline for one task, cursor-paginated in eventId order. Deterministic: pages never overlap and never skip; an unknown task is TASK_NOT_FOUND.

cursor.description: Last eventId the caller has already seen for this task; 0 starts from the beginning of the task's history.

items.description: Durable event envelopes for this task, in strictly increasing eventId order.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page; null when end-of-history was reached (truncated=false).

truncated.description: true when more events exist beyond this page (end-of-history is truncated=false with no further events after nextCursor).

staleCursor.description: true when the requested cursor precedes the node's retained event window; the page starts at the earliest retained event for this task and the response is partial.

FileWriteRequest.description: Optimistic concurrency: the client supplies baseVersion/baseHash from its last read; mismatch yields CONFLICT with the current remote state.

overwrite.description: Explicit overwrite; audited; still refuses to clobber a newer file silently.

FileReadRequest.description: Reads one workspace file. Every read returns content, version, hash, modifiedAt (PROTOCOL §7).

version.description: Monotonic file version on the node.

FileBrowseRequest.description: Lists one directory of a project workspace. Paths are resolved and validated server-side; traversal attempts are rejected before any filesystem access.

path.description: Directory relative to the workspace root; null or '' means the root.

TerminalRequest.description: Requires the 'terminal' scope. Command and session ids are audit-logged; output is redacted of known secret patterns. Bounded by timeoutMs.

env.description: Sanitized; never contains credentials from the vault.

TerminalCancelRequest.description: Cancels a running terminal execution by its terminal id.

DiagnosticsRunRequest.description: Runs node doctor checks. Returns DiagnosticsResult. Repair is a separate, explicitly-scoped operation not implemented in v1 desktop.

checks.description: Optional subset of check ids; omitted means all checks.

recommendedAction.description: Safe action text, possibly a repair command.

DeviceRevokeRequest.description: Revokes a paired device. Immediate for new connections; any live stream for that device is closed at the next event boundary.

forget.description: true also removes the device record (status 'forgotten'); false keeps it as 'revoked'.

missing.description: true when the registered workspace directory is absent from the drive.

ProjectCreateRequest.description: Registers a project in the portable workspace registry. path=null creates a project directory under the portable drive.

path.description: External workspace to bind; null creates under data/projects.

ProjectOpenRequest.description: Opens a registered project and returns its resolved workspace path and metadata.

SessionView.description: Universal Harness session metadata (the orchestration record; never conversation content). dshAvailable reports whether the underlying dsh conversation store currently holds a session under this id.

status.description: 'open' or a terminal marker; the node owns this lifecycle.

dshAvailable.description: true when the node's dsh session store holds a conversation with this id.

SessionCreateRequest.description: Creates a harness session for a project. This registers Universal Harness orchestration metadata only; the dsh conversation itself is created by dsh when the first task runs against the session.

SessionReadRequest.description: Reads one session: Universal Harness metadata, plus — clearly separated — what the node can actually read from the dsh conversation store (summary metadata, and optionally a bounded transcript page). The node never invents dsh data; when dsh has no conversation under this id, dsh.available is false and nothing is fabricated.

includeTranscript.description: Include one page of the dsh conversation log (requires dsh.available).

limit.description: Transcript page size when includeTranscript is true.

cursor.description: Transcript continuation cursor (the previous page's nextTranscriptCursor); null starts from the beginning.

items.description: Raw dsh conversation log lines (JSONL entries as stored by dsh), in seq order.

nextTranscriptCursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the next transcript page; null when no more pages are known.

DshSessionInfo.description: What Universal Harness can truthfully report about the dsh-owned conversation. Universal Harness reads this store; it never writes it.

available.description: false when dsh has no conversation under this session id (e.g. created but no task has run yet); no other field is meaningful then.

incomplete.description: true when dsh's last turn never reached turn/end (process died mid-turn).

SessionResumeRequest.description: Linked continuation. Universal Harness CANNOT reopen a persisted dsh conversation in place (the dsh SDK seam creates sessions; it does not reopen stored ones), so resume creates a NEW session whose priorSessionId links back to the requested one. The dsh conversation is NOT reopened and no conversation content is copied; the lineage metadata is the continuation. Task work submitted against the new session runs in a fresh dsh conversation under the new id.

SessionResumeResponse.description: The new continuation session. resumedFromSessionId makes the lineage explicit on the wire.

version.description: Target version; null = latest verified manifest entry.

ReplayResponse.description: Response to session.replay with lastEventId. Returns durable events strictly after the cursor. If the durable store cannot serve beyond the cursor (retention exceeded, corrupted index, fresh install), the node sets unavailable=true and returns an authoritative RecoverySnapshot instead; clients reconcile from it and must never infer task state from the mere absence of events.

items.description: Envelopes with eventId; durable events only.

unavailable.description: true when the node cannot serve events beyond the given cursor. Clients must then rely on the provided RecoverySnapshot.

RecoverySnapshot.description: Authoritative point-in-time node state used when event replay is unavailable or after ambiguous crash windows. Doubles as the reconciliation baseline. Contains only task/session metadata, never conversation content.

recovered.description: true if the state was re-derived by the supervisor after an abnormal termination rather than read from a persisted record.
